amenitiesDescription: The Residences at Mandarin Oriental, Miami sits atop a 100,000 SF landscaped resort podium, among the most expansive of any Brickell Key new development. South Tower residents access an Ocean Pool with five cabanas, a Lagoon Pool with six private villas (kitchenettes, en-suite baths, sun decks), immersive forest walk, rotating art walk, indoor golf simulator, private screening lounge, game room, kids' club, outdoor Dining Pavilion with grill, Tea Pavilion, glass-encased private dining room with chef's kitchen and wine cellar, and a full business suite. North Tower residents add a 19th-level Residents Lounge with chef's kitchen and private dining, plus complete access to Mandarin Oriental's flagship hotel amenities: signature spa with hammam, saunas, vitality and lap pools, wellness lawn, Technogym fitness atelier, three restaurants, and children's splash pad. All residents receive dedicated concierge service and preferred status across Mandarin Oriental's global hotel portfolio.
architectQuote: Brickell Key is unlike any site in Miami: entirely surrounded by water. Every decision we made was in service of that extraordinary fact.
description: Mandarin Oriental's five-star service returns to Brickell Key. Two KPF towers, 326 residences. Swire broke ground October 2026. Record penthouses at ~$50M each. Over $1.7B sold before groundbreaking. Completion 2030.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Mandarin Oriental Residences is the most compelling combination of scarcity, brand, and protected views in the Miami market. Swire's long land tenure means pricing is below what a competitor would pay to replicate this island position today. Over $1.7B in sales before groundbreaking, including both ~$50M penthouses, and a largely domestic buyer base keep the 2030 delivery path intact while South Tower primary inventory tightens.

investmentThesis: Mandarin Oriental's first North American flagship in over a decade, and Swire Properties' first branded residential development globally. Total sales surpassed $1.7B before groundbreaking, with the South Tower 80% sold and the North Tower at 25%. Asking prices are up about 30% since the 2024 South Tower launch, and roughly 65% of buyers are domestic. The Wall Street Journal reported two 66th-floor duplex penthouses under contract at $49.9M each. Swire (Brickell City Centre, One Island Drive) broke ground October 2026, less than six months after the April hotel implosion, self-financing construction from City Centre asset sales and buyer deposits, with delivery targeted for 2030. The island is functionally built-out: this site replaces the only hotel parcel, and no comparable land remains.

residenceContent: Brickell Key is the only entirely water-surrounded site in Miami's urban core, and the architecture by KPF is built around that fact. The 66-story South Tower delivers 228 residences from 2 to 5 bedrooms (2,333–5,800 SF), virtually all corner units, with interiors by Parisian designer Tristan Auer. Residences feature 10-to-12-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling glass, dual private elevator access, full-depth terraces, Italian stone flooring, Gaggenau appliances, and integrated smart home systems. The 33-story North Tower adds 70 private residences and 28 Hotel Collection residences with interiors by Laura Gonzalez, sitting alongside Mandarin Oriental's new North American flagship hotel (121 guestrooms).
